question.text: A wire having a linear mass density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>9</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> is stretched between two rigid supports with a tension of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>900</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The wire resonates at a frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The next higher frequency at which the same wire resonates is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>550</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi><mo>.</mo></math> The length of the wire is ___________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo>.</mo></math>
